editorial:
Imagine a movie that mixes real-life facts with cool drawings to tell a story about a very special character. You get to meet Norm, and the whole vibe is just warm, cozy, and genuinely sweet. It feels less like a big studio production and more like a passion project made by someone who really cares about the subject. The way it blends documentary elements with animation makes it feel fresh, keeping you interested without feeling like you are sitting through a boring school lesson. It is the kind of short film that makes you smile and think about the little things in life.

What really makes this work is the pacing; it does not overstay its welcome and gets straight to the heart of the story. While it is a short piece, the art style is a huge plus and keeps your eyes glued to the screen. If you have a few spare minutes, you should definitely check this out.
endingExplained: The film wraps up by showing you the true impact Norm had on the people around him. In the final scenes, the animation blends back into real footage to show that while the story is short, the memory of Norm lasts forever. There is no huge shock twist, but the emotional payoff comes when you realize Norm represents a feeling of kindness. It ends on a hopeful note, leaving you feeling happy and peaceful.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves short stories and creative animation.
